newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong, United States sign extradition pact.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong, United States sign extradition pact.

text.p: Hong Kong and the United States on Friday signed an extradition agreement that will prevent Hong Kong from sending crime suspects to a third jurisdiction after the British colony reverts to China next year.
The agreement, which has been endorsed by Beijing, also contains provisions to allow refusal to extradite fugitives accused of political offences.

"The act reflects America's support for Hong Kong's high degree of autonomy, including the independence of the legal and judicial system, after the territory's reversion to China next July," U.S. Consul General Richard Boucher said at the signing.
Concern that suspects extradited to Hong Kong may end up in China's judicial system has become an issue in the run up to the territory's handover next year.

In November, lawyers for a former British American Tobacco Co executive argued in U.S. District Court that their client should not be extradited to Hong Kong on bribery charges because he would face possible execution after the handover.
A decision is due before the end of the year.

The Hong Kong-U.S. agreement contains standard safeguards, including that the act for which a person's return is requested must be a crime in both jurisdictions, return may be refused for political offences, and resurrender to a third jurisdiction requires the consent of the requested person.
